author: claude
desc: Three defects in how t6040-boot-raw-object.sh invoked chainload.py, all of which cost rig time on 2026-07-26. (1) ORPHANS: the `timeout` wrapper was reparented to init when the script's parent was killed and its python child kept running; one such orphan had pushed ~41 MiB into the KIS pty and then sat holding it, silently corrupting the maintainer's next TWO runs — the target stayed at 'Running proxy' because two writers interleaved on one transport, and the symptom was misread as the machine being stuck. (2) NO PROGRESS: python block-buffers stdout to a file, so the log stayed 0 bytes until exit and a healthy upload was indistinguishable from a hang. (3) FIXED 300s TIMEOUT: measured KIS rate is ~0.7 MB/s, and the capability-first policy (155) makes objects larger, not smaller.
result: 2026-07-26 FIXED, orphan prevention proven by test. (1) `set -m` puts the chainload job in its own process group and an EXIT/INT/TERM trap kills the WHOLE group, so no wrapper or child survives the script. Verified offline with a sleep-based stand-in: before SIGTERM both 'timeout 300' and its child were alive; after SIGTERM of the parent, both were gone. NOTE this covers SIGTERM/SIGINT (what a tool timeout or Ctrl-C sends) but cannot cover SIGKILL, where no trap can run. (2) PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 makes the log fill live, and the script now prints the object size plus a 'tail -f <log>' hint, so progress is observable instead of inferred from CPU time. (3) Timeout is now 120s + 5s/MiB, overridable with T6040_CHAINLOAD_TIMEOUT. Accuracy note: the old fixed 300s was MARGINAL BUT SUFFICIENT for the 79 MiB fat object (measured ~120s), so it was not the cause of any failure today; it would however genuinely fail the 512 MiB probe of ticket 156, which needs ~730s at the measured rate. Scaled values: 9 MiB->165s, 79 MiB->515s, 512 MiB->2680s.
